item.text:
Completed the bounded 1B continuation research. No score assigned.

Recovered evidence:

- IAEA’s 2023 safeguards statement confirms safeguards conclusions were based on independent verification and all relevant information, but the accessible material did not expose a Vietnam-specific conclusion. This supports retaining formal safeguards evidence while marking country-specific implementation unresolved. [IAEA Safeguards Statement 2023](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/24/06/20240607_sir_2024_part_ab.pdf)

- Vietnam’s radioactive-source system had material inherited weaknesses: approximately 5,300 sealed sources, insufficient long-term storage, six reported source-loss incidents since 2005, loose facility controls, and historically slow emergency coordination. This is adverse technical context, not a 2023 incident finding. [IAEA conference paper on Vietnam](https://conferences.iaea.org/event/181/contributions/15809/)

- Vietnam’s 2023 AI-readiness score rose to 54.48 and ranked fifth in Southeast Asia, measuring government, technology-sector, and data/infrastructure capability. It does not establish catastrophic-risk safeguards or independent oversight. [Government report on the 2023 AI Readiness Index](https://en.baochinhphu.vn/viet-nam-ranks-5-in-southeast-asia-in-government-ai-readiness-index-11124011621452292.htm)

- Freedom House documents 2023 platform takedown pressure, Decree 53 enforcement, and imprisonment for online activity, strengthening the adverse evidence on cyber governance, privacy, and independent vulnerability scrutiny. [Freedom on the Net 2023](https://freedomhouse.org/country/vietnam/freedom-net/2023)
